title: U.S. House · Indiana's 3rd District
area: Northeast Indiana, including Fort Wayne and surrounding counties

context.text: Incumbent Marlin A. Stutzman won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Jon Kenworthy. Kelly Thompson won the Democratic primary. Phillip Beachy is running as an independent write-in candidate, as he did in 2024.

candidates.name: Marlin A. Stutzman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Jon Kenworthy

summary.text: Marlin Stutzman is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 3rd District. A fourth-generation farmer from Howe, he served in the Indiana House and Senate and in the U.S. House beginning in 2010, worked in manufacturing, agriculture and food-service businesses during a break from Congress, and returned to the U.S. House in 2025. He is seeking re-election to the seat.

background.text: Born in Sturgis, Michigan, in 1976; graduated from Lake Area Christian High School and attended Trine State University.

According to his official biography, he is a fourth-generation farmer from Howe, Indiana, who started his own beef cattle operation at 16 and by 18 had joined his father and other family members in growing the family business.

Elected to the Indiana House of Representatives at age 25 as its youngest serving member, serving from 2002 to 2008 while working full time in the family business; his official biography says he helped Gov. Mitch Daniels turn a $1 billion deficit into a surplus.
Served one term in the Indiana State Senate (2009-2010).

Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2010. His official biography says he authored the Conservative Congressional Budget and was the original sponsor of the Right to Try legislation, later signed into law by President Trump.

After leaving Congress, worked as an entrepreneur in manufacturing, agriculture and food service; he and his wife, Christy, previously owned a farm-to-fork dinner theater with a meat processing facility that raised Wagyu beef, according to his official biography.
Returned to the U.S. House in 2025 and serves on the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress.
Is a member of the LaGrange Chamber of Commerce, National Federation of Independent Business, Indiana Farm Bureau, the Howe Community Association and the National Rifle Association.

priorities.text: Describes the One Big Beautiful Bill Act as the start of a return to fiscal discipline in federal spending.
priorities.quote: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act is the start of America’s return to fiscal sanity.

priorities.text: Says regulatory barriers between HUD and USDA housing programs should be removed to make it easier and cheaper to build affordable housing.
priorities.quote: we must remove the barriers that drive up costs and make it harder to build housing for Americans who need it most

priorities.text: Introduced legislation to increase mandatory minimum sentences for fentanyl trafficking.

positions.summary: Introduced the Streamlining Rural Housing Act, which directs HUD and USDA to align environmental review and inspection standards for rural housing projects, saying it would make affordable housing easier to build.
positions.quote: we must remove the barriers that drive up costs and make it harder to build housing for Americans who need it most

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on the Budget for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the Budget Committee and Financial Services Committee during an earlier term in the 114th Congress (2015-2016).

Introduced the Streamlining Rural Housing Act with Reps. Brittany Pettersen, Lisa McClain, and David Scott, directing HUD and USDA to evaluate a joint environmental review and inspection process for rural housing projects.
Introduced the No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act, the House companion to Sen. John Kennedy's Fairness in Fentanyl Sentencing Act.

summary.text: Kelly Thompson is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 3rd District. Describing herself as a Hoosier business owner and nonprofit founder, she has worked as a substitute teacher and jail-ministry visiting pastor and ran unsuccessfully for the Indiana House in 2020. She is running on a platform that includes public education and the cost of living for working families.

background.text: Born in Palo Alto, California; graduated salutatorian from Tippecanoe Valley High School in Indiana.
Attended Valparaiso University's Christ College before moving to Florida with her family and earning a BS in Business Administration from the University of Central Florida (1989).
Describes herself as a Hoosier business owner and nonprofit founder; Ballotpedia lists her career experience as business owner.
Outside her business, has worked as a substitute teacher and as a visiting pastor of a local jail ministry, according to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
Says she spent over a decade volunteering to help local teens and families through a nonprofit she founded.
Was the Democratic candidate for Indiana House District 22 in 2020 and lost the general election.
Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary for Indiana's 3rd District unopposed.

priorities.text: Says working families struggle to afford housing, food, medical care, and education, and blames policymakers who she says do not feel that pain.
Says she would move toward a single-payer healthcare system, citing medical debt as a leading cause of bankruptcy.
priorities.quote: We can reduce that to 5% by moving to a single payor system.

priorities.text: Campaign website proposes a federal program to keep family farmland from being sold to corporations or foreign governments, exempting family-to-family land transfers from the estate tax.

positions.summary: Says she supports moving to a single-payer healthcare system to reduce the share of income Americans spend on medical costs.
positions.quote: It's time to provide heath care to everyone regardless of our net worth.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for zoning reform to allow greater density, legalizing accessory dwelling units, and streamlining permitting to increase housing supply.
Proposes a 2-cent tax on stock, bond, commodity, and derivative trades on Wall Street to fund education and pre-K programs.
Campaign material references raising teacher pay and worker income as part of her education and economic platform.

candidates.name: Phillip Beachy
candidates.ballotNote: Independent write-in candidate; also ran as a write-in in 2024

summary.text: Phillip Beachy is a Fort Wayne native, semi-retired carpenter and refrigeration technician who owns EcoThunder Refrigeration. He is an independent write-in candidate for Indiana's 3rd District and was also a write-in candidate for U.S. Senate in 2024.

background.text: Born in Fort Wayne, Indiana; graduated from Woodland High School.
Works as a semi-retired carpenter and refrigerator technician and owns EcoThunder Refrigeration.
Appeared as an independent write-in candidate in the 2024 U.S. Senate election in Indiana, receiving 168 votes.

priorities.text: Says the Citizens United decision was wrong and should be overturned, and criticizes the influence of money in government.
priorities.quote: The influence of money in our system of government is out of control, the Citizens United decision was wrong and must be overturned.

priorities.text: Says he would end subsidies to oil and auto companies and favors more SNAP spending.
priorities.quote: We must end the billions in subsidies to the oil companies, auto companies, and other industries. More SNAP less gas.

positions.summary: Says the budget could be balanced with a 50% top marginal tax rate, closing loopholes, affecting only the top 10% of earners.
positions.quote: I believe we can balance the budget with a 50% top marginal rate if we get rid of loopholes. My rates would only affect the 10%.

positions.summary: Says raising the minimum wage to the inflation-adjusted equivalent of 1974 levels (about $12.50) would help younger workers and Social Security solvency.

researchNotes: Marlin Stutzman has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; his stutzman.house.gov Issues pages (Congress, Economy, Education, Energy, Health, Veterans) and stutzmanforcongress.com were checked. Positions and priorities are drawn from official press releases; his committee record is documented as well. No campaign website was located for Beachy beyond his Candidate Connection survey answers. Beachy's public biography is limited to his Ballotpedia entry; Thompson's and Stutzman's pre-2002 careers are described only briefly in the sources found.
